title: Legal controls on marketing
notes: Authored 2026-10-06 under standard v0.2.0-draft. All claims are provenance generated_gap, verification unverified.

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Explain how legal controls on marketing - against misleading promotion and over faulty and dangerous goods - shape what a business may claim, sell and plan.

blocks.heading: What legal controls are
blocks.text: Legal controls on marketing are laws that restrict what businesses may claim in their promotion and require the goods they sell to be safe, of acceptable quality and as described. Two areas concern marketing most. Misleading promotion: an advert, label or price claim may not deceive consumers about what the product does, what it costs or how its price compares. Faulty and dangerous goods: products may not injure the user, and a product that breaks or burns is in breach of the law whatever its advertising said.

blocks.heading: From rule to strategy
blocks.text: The rule changes the plan, and the chain runs from compliance to cost to customer trust. Condition: a Namibian importer of electric kettles learns that every model must pass a safety test before it may be stocked. Mechanism: testing adds cost and delay to each launch, so the importer’s marketing strategy budgets for it - promotions are scheduled after the certificate arrives, and the safer model’s higher price is explained on the label rather than hidden. Consequence for the business: launches run slower and cost more, but the importer can point to tested products, and shoppers who trust the label tend to keep buying. The chain also runs against the business that gambles: a European toy maker forced to recall a batch with detachable small parts paid for the recall, the lost shelf time and the publicity at once, and the fines were the smallest part of the bill. One boundary to keep: following the law is what is demanded; marketing ethically - such as choosing not to aim sugary-drink adverts at children - is a choice the law may not force.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: Topic 2.3 meets legal controls again over employment - contracts, discrimination and health and safety at work. Topic 6.2 separates legal duties from ethical choices more fully. Topic 3.3’s promotion methods are the tools these controls constrain: whatever the channel, the claim has to be honest and the product safe.
